name: Synthetic Chemistry
tagline: Engineering molecules with purpose through multistep synthesis and automation.
seo_title: Synthetic Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Synthetic Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in total synthesis, new reactions, asymmetric synthesis and automated synthesis.

definition.lead: Synthetic chemistry is the science of building molecules on purpose, from simple starting materials to complex targets.
definition.body: Nearly every medicine, pesticide, dye and advanced material started in a synthesis lab. Chemists plan routes, choose reactions, control selectivity and scale up, increasingly with the help of automation and AI.

facts.label: Wöhler makes urea, an organic compound, from an inorganic salt
the total synthesis of vitamin B12 is completed by Woodward and Eschenmoser
Nobel Prize to E. J. Corey for the theory and methodology of organic synthesis

branches.name: Total synthesis
branches.summary: Building complex natural products entirely from simple materials.
branches.example: Taxol, the anticancer drug from yew bark.

branches.name: Methodology
branches.summary: Inventing new reactions that make bonds faster, cleaner or more selectively.
branches.example: C–H activation turns ordinary C–H bonds into reactive handles.

branches.name: Route planning
branches.summary: Designing the sequence of steps from the target backwards.

branches.name: Asymmetric synthesis
branches.example: Chiral catalysts that give a single enantiomer.

branches.name: Process chemistry
branches.summary: Turning a lab route into a safe, cheap, large-scale process.
branches.example: Manufacturing a drug by the tonne.

branches.name: Flow chemistry
branches.summary: Running reactions continuously in tubes instead of flasks.
branches.example: Handling hazardous intermediates in tiny volumes.

branches.name: Automated synthesis
branches.summary: Machines that run reactions and purifications.

branches.name: Ring construction
branches.summary: Building the ring systems found in drugs and natural products.

timeline.title: Urea from an inorganic salt
timeline.text: Friedrich Wöhler heats ammonium cyanate and obtains urea.
timeline.why: An early sign that organic compounds can be made in the lab.

timeline.title: The first synthetic dye
timeline.text: William Perkin, aged 18, tries to make quinine and obtains mauveine instead.

timeline.title: Aspirin
timeline.text: Chemists at Bayer prepare acetylsalicylic acid in a pure, stable form.
timeline.why: One of the first mass-produced synthetic drugs.

timeline.title: A one-pot alkaloid
timeline.text: Robert Robinson makes tropinone from simple materials in a single operation.
timeline.why: A landmark of elegant, biomimetic synthesis.

timeline.title: Quinine
timeline.text: Robert Woodward and William Doering report a formal total synthesis of quinine.
timeline.why: Showed that complex natural products were within reach.

timeline.title: Solid-phase synthesis
timeline.text: Bruce Merrifield builds peptides on a solid support, step by step.
timeline.why: Made peptide synthesis fast and automatable; Nobel Prize in 1984.

timeline.title: The art of synthesis
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Robert Burns Woodward for his achievements in organic synthesis.
timeline.why: Synthesis recognized as a creative discipline.

timeline.title: Vitamin B12
timeline.text: Woodward and Albert Eschenmoser complete the synthesis of vitamin B12 after more than a decade, with about 100 co-workers.
timeline.why: One of the most complex syntheses ever attempted at the time.

timeline.title: Taxol
timeline.text: The groups of Robert Holton and K. C. Nicolaou report total syntheses of the anticancer drug Taxol.

timeline.title: Cross-coupling
timeline.text: Nobel Prize to Heck, Negishi and Suzuki for palladium-catalysed cross-couplings.
timeline.why: Now among the most used reactions in drug discovery.

quiz.explain: Woodward synthesized quinine, cholesterol, chlorophyll and more.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of flow chemistry?
options: Small volumes and precise control make hazardous reactions safer
It needs no reagents at all
It needs no energy input of any kind
It is always faster than batch chemistry

quiz.q: Why is Robinson's 1917 tropinone synthesis famous?
options: It built a complex alkaloid in one pot from simple materials
It was the first synthesis done without water
It made the first synthetic polymer
It used electricity to drive every step
quiz.explain: It imitated the way plants are thought to make the molecule.
